newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends down 1.06 in quiet markets.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends down 1.06 in quiet markets.

text.p: Colombia's peso fell back 1.06 to 994.6 to the dollar as Thanksgiving Day in the United States coupled with expectation over 1997 macroeconomic targets, due for release Friday, dulled markets.
Interbank dealers reported 95 trades worth a total of $43.2 million. The peso hit an intra-day high of 994.3 to the dollar and a low of 995.2.

"There was a bit of a speculative trend in the markets. Some institutions tried to make a quick profit before month-end. They are looking for the peso to fall lower than last month's rate so that they don't have to report losses," one Bogota trader said.
Another dealer said many potential clients preferred to stay away given that a central bank announcement on 1997 devaluation and inflation targets was imminent.
"Everybody is holding their breath in expectation of the central bank figures due Friday," the dealer said.
In a speech Thursday, co-director of the central bank Roberto Junguito said the bank would set a target for peso devaluation of between 13 and 15 percent in nominal terms.
Interbank dealers said the dollar was likely to come under renewed downward pressure Friday as foreign export earnings enter the markets.
